records.title: linux wayland crash
records.reason: Not reproduced, and the shell was reached rather than assumed. A native build was produced here (`apps/desktop/src-tauri` is outside the root workspace, and its build script needs the ONNX runtime artifacts fetched by `scripts/fetch-onnxruntime.mjs`). Launched against this session's Wayland compositor, the app opens a window and renders its real UI — menubar, Layers panel, Inspector and the first-run "Get Help Anytime" dialog — and stays alive until killed, with only a benign `gtk_window_set_titlebar() called on a realized window` warning. records.reason: Opening an oversized `.fig` fails with a named limit instead of exhausting memory. Varve budgets the import explicitly — 64 MB bytes, 100 000 nodes, depth 256, 2 M characters of text — and both the JSON and native `.fig` paths enforce them with actionable messages that name the limit. `figmaLimits.test.ts` pins the node ceiling, the depth ceiling, the native byte ceiling (checked before any decoding, so it fails fast) and a normal file that must still import. records.title: bug: Closing an unsaved document (X button) discards work silently, no save prompt
records.varveWorkflow: Lifecycle / termination coordinator, tab close guard, autosave
records.finding: Dirty state had two flags. `state.dirty` and `sessions[].dirty` were written by different code paths, and several mutation helpers set only the state flag. The close guard and termination collector read the session flag, so a real edit could close or quit with no prompt, and the recovery point was deleted on the resulting clean shutdown. `useLogoGeometry` writes the document with no transaction at all.
records.outcome: One authority (`markDocumentDirty`) for the unsaved flag, a document setter that applies it, and a reconciliation guard for hand-written sites.
records.evidence: commit 13014f0ed; unsavedWorkAuthority.test.tsx — the stale-state shape yields zero documents for `collectUnsavedDocuments`

records.title: bug: undo keyboard shortcut does not match keyboad layout
records.finding: Undo shortcut vs keyboard layout. Not investigated in this pass.
records.reason: Shortcut matching is layout-correct by construction. A dedicated physical-key module resolves digits and numpad keys from KeyboardEvent.code (so Shift+1 and NumLock states behave), while letters resolve from KeyboardEvent.key — the printed character — which is what a user reading their own keycaps expects for Ctrl+Z on AZERTY or QWERTZ. The single implementation is shared by the global registry and the canvas-local handler.
